description: Phase 2A archive ingestion policy — profile-driven decisions for compressed sources. Determines copy-as-payload vs extract-then-classify vs grouped vs manual_review vs unsupported. All extraction in temp workspace, never to SD.

.7z.note: Abstraction already exists; planner will return unsupported_archive without rewriting planner when handler becomes available.

defaults.comment: Global fallback when no per-system rule matches. Most archives are containers that should be extracted and classified.

payload.description: archive-is-payload: copy the archive file intact to its system folder; do NOT extract.

container.description: archive-is-container: archive is a delivery container; contents are independent files. Extract-then-classify each member.
container.note: Legacy alias for extract_and_classify; kept for backwards compat.

extract_and_classify.description: Default: extract safely to temp workspace, then classify each member via systems/media/bios profiles as if it were a loose file.

grouped.description: grouped multi-file payload: members that form one logical game (e.g., CUE+BIN, chd + cue) must be kept together. Planner operates on logical units, not individual files.

manual.description: unresolved/manual review: ambiguous, mixed, or policy-undecided. Planner returns manual_review for explicit user decision.

unsupported.description: Format recognized but handler not available in this runtime/tooling. Returns unsupported_archive.

cue_bin.description: Any .cue with sibling .bin files forms one logical unit. Includes archive members: a directory containing game.cue + game.bin (+ maybe .img) is grouped.
cue_bin.action: single planner entry with group members

m3u.description: M3U playlist referencing multiple disc images -> grouped

nested_archive.description: Archive inside archive (depth > max_depth) -> manual_review, not automatic bomb extraction.

collision.description: Two members would collide to same destination path (case-insensitive on Windows, case-sensitive on SD). Detect and return manual_review or conflict instead of silent overwrite.
collision.strategy: normalize lowercased dest path + collision map

rationale: Why profile-driven instead of globally extracting every archive: Some TreeFrog content MUST remain compressed. Arcade romsets (cps1/neogeo/m2k) are validated as .zip payloads per core; extracting them would break core loading. Other systems (NES/SNES/GBA) traditionally accept both loose and .zip but user may want to preserve .zip as-is for some sets. Hardcoding ZIP=>always extract in scanner would be wrong and not portable across devices. Profile-driven policy keeps scanner generic, planner deterministic, and allows future per-system tuning without rewriting planner. See DECISIONS.md DEC-2026-08-28-02.
